statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-129483: the SRP server mechanism of Cyrus SASL through 2.1.28 does not reject a client public value A that is a multiple of N in srp_server_mech_step2, so an unauthenticated client can force a zero shared secret and authenticate as any existing user without the password. It is reported at https://github.com/cyrusimap/cyrus-sasl/issues/896, and upstream removed the SRP plugin (plugins/srp.c) in https://github.com/cyrusimap/cyrus-sasl/commit/fb3724f43dc50247ff2bf02135457d6d77031654. The vulnerable code is not in this package. Debian builds cyrus-sasl2 with --disable-srp (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-129483), and the DHI packages are rebuilds of Debian's 2.1.28+dfsg1-9. Unpacked all 102 binary packages published from the cyrus-sasl2 source in the DHI Debian repository, its three published rebuilds for amd64 and arm64: libsasl2-2, libsasl2-modules, libsasl2-modules-db, libsasl2-modules-gssapi-mit, libsasl2-modules-gssapi-heimdal, libsasl2-modules-ldap, libsasl2-modules-otp, libsasl2-dev and sasl2-bin, and their debug-symbol packages. The mechanism plugins in /usr/lib/<triplet>/sasl2/ are anonymous, crammd5, digestmd5, gs2, gssapiv2, ldapdb, login, ntlm, otp, plain, sasldb and scram; there is no SRP plugin. The static archive libsasl2.a in libsasl2-dev holds the library's and those plugins' object files and no srp object. No program, shared library, static archive or debug file contains the SRP plugin's symbols, such as srp_server_mech_step2 or srp_server_plug_init. The programs and libraries are ELF files dynamically linked against the system libc.so.6, and the debug-symbol packages hold detached debug information.
